pages.title: Not Yet in Bloom
pages.text:
The garden does not keep a clock.
One flower opens; others wait.
Beneath the soil, a quiet root
can grow without a single cheer.

I need not race the morning light
or borrow someone else's spring.
My steady effort has a place.
Not yet in bloom is still alive.
pages.translation:
정원은 시계를 보지 않아요.
한 꽃이 피어나고, 다른 꽃들은 기다려요.
흙 아래 조용한 뿌리는
응원 한마디 없이도 자랄 수 있어요.

아침 햇살과 경주할 필요도,
다른 누군가의 봄을 빌릴 필요도 없어요.
꾸준히 기울이는 내 노력에도 자리가 있어요.
아직 꽃피지 않았어도, 여전히 살아 있어요.
pages.scene: An original editorial watercolor and gouache illustration for teenagers: a quiet school garden at dawn, one open flower and several closed buds, subtle cutaway soil showing strong growing roots. A thoughtful Korean teenager with short black hair watches from a bench. Muted sage green, dusty rose and warm cream. Mature, poetic, no cute mascots.

pages.title: The Result
pages.text: When I received my science test, I looked only at the grade. It was lower than I expected. Around me, friends compared their results. I folded the paper and hid it inside my book. I had spent a whole week preparing. For a moment, that single number seemed to say that all my effort had been a waste.
pages.translation: 과학 시험지를 받았을 때, 나는 점수만 보았다. 기대보다 낮은 점수였다. 주변에서는 친구들이 서로 결과를 비교했다. 나는 시험지를 접어 책 속에 숨겼다. 꼬박 일주일을 준비했는데, 순간 그 숫자 하나 때문에 그동안의 노력이 모두 헛수고처럼 느껴졌다.
pages.scene: Mature young-adult editorial gouache illustration, muted indigo and warm cream: a Korean teenage girl with chin-length straight black hair and a plain navy school cardigan sits at a school desk, quietly folding a test paper into an open book while classmates talk in the soft-focus background. Sensitive restrained expression, no readable grades or other lettering.

pages.title: A New Question
pages.text: That evening, I opened my notebook again. I found a clear chart, a clear record of an experiment, and a question I had once been afraid to ask. None of these appeared in the final grade. Instead of asking why I was not perfect, I asked what I could understand better. The question gave me a way forward.
pages.translation: 그날 저녁, 나는 공책을 다시 펼쳤다. 알아보기 쉽게 그린 도표와 꼼꼼한 실험 기록, 그리고 한때 묻기 두려웠던 질문이 눈에 들어왔다. 점수만 봐서는 알 수 없는 것들이었다. 완벽하지 못한 이유를 묻는 대신, 어떤 부분을 더 공부하면 좋을지 생각했다. 그렇게 생각하니 다음에 할 일이 보였다.
pages.scene: Same Korean teenage girl, chin-length straight black hair and plain navy cardigan, at her bedroom desk in evening lamplight, studying a notebook with a simple chart and science sketches. Mature young-adult editorial gouache, indigo blue, amber and warm cream, thoughtful hopeful expression, no readable lettering.

pages.title: What Remained
pages.text: The next day, I asked for advice and worked through one difficult problem with a friend. My grade did not change, but my attitude did. A result can show where I need practice; it cannot measure my entire future. Now I keep that test beside my notes. It reminds me to value progress, accept help, and continue learning.
pages.translation: 다음 날, 나는 조언을 구하고 친구와 함께 어려운 문제 하나를 차근차근 풀었다. 점수는 그대로였지만 내 태도는 달라졌다. 시험 결과로 무엇을 더 연습해야 할지는 알 수 있다. 하지만 그 점수가 내 미래까지 정해 주는 건 아니다. 이제 나는 그 시험지를 필기 옆에 둔다. 조금씩 나아지는 걸 소중히 여기고, 필요할 땐 도움을 받으며 계속 배워 가자는 마음을 잊지 않으려고 한다.
pages.scene: Same Korean teenage girl with chin-length black hair and a plain navy cardigan, working together with a teenage friend over a science notebook in a bright school library. Mature editorial gouache with soft daylight, indigo, sage and warm cream, hopeful and respectful, no childish mascots and no readable text.

pages.title: The Message
pages.text: At eleven, the machine in our school laboratory produced a photograph. Our science coach had built it to receive messages, not pictures. The photograph showed a note in my own writing: 'Do not open the gate at noon. Ask for help.' Below it was tomorrow's date. I checked my watch. We had one hour before the first test of the gate.
pages.translation: 열한 시, 학교 실험실의 기계가 사진 한 장을 출력했다. 선생님이 메시지를 받으려고 만든 기계인데, 사진이 나온 것이었다. 사진에는 내 필체로 쓴 쪽지가 찍혀 있었다. '낮 열두 시에 문을 열지 마. 도와 달라고 해.' 그 아래에는 내일 날짜가 있었다. 나는 시계를 확인했다. 문을 처음 시험하기까지 한 시간이 남아 있었다.
pages.scene: Original young-adult science-fiction gouache illustration, atmospheric teal and amber: a Korean teenage boy with short black hair, navy school blazer and a simple silver wristwatch holds a freshly printed photograph beside a compact brass-and-teal signal receiver. Behind him is a dormant oval experimental gate made of two metal arcs in a realistic school laboratory. Printed photo has indistinct handwriting, no legible extra text. Tense but not horror.

pages.title: A Simple Trick?
pages.text: My friend studied the photograph. 'Someone knows your writing,' she said. 'It could be a trick.' She was right. A strange message was not evidence of the future. Still, I could not ignore it. We called our science coach, who was preparing the test in another room. She asked us to bring the photograph and leave every switch alone.
pages.translation: 친구가 사진을 살펴보았다. '누군가 네 글씨를 아는 거야. 장난일 수도 있어.' 친구 말이 맞았다. 이상한 메시지를 받았다고 해서 미래에서 왔다고 믿을 수는 없었다. 그래도 무시할 수는 없었다. 우리는 다른 방에서 시험을 준비하던 선생님께 연락했다. 선생님은 스위치를 건드리지 말고 사진을 가져오라고 하셨다.
pages.scene: Same original Korean teenage boy with short black hair, navy blazer, silver wristwatch, and his friend, a Korean teenage girl with a black ponytail and gray cardigan, examining a photograph while using a school laboratory wall telephone. Brass-and-teal receiver and dormant twin-arc oval gate in background. Young-adult SF gouache, teal shadows and amber daylight, no logos or extra text.

pages.title: Beneath the Table
pages.text: On the way out, my friend stopped. A thin line of smoke rose beneath the gate's table. We did not touch anything. From the door, we could see a cable pressed under a heavy metal box. Our science coach arrived, moved us into the hall, and called an engineer. The photograph might be wrong. The smoke was real.
pages.translation: 나가던 길에 친구가 멈춰 섰다. 문이 놓인 실험대 아래에서 가느다란 연기가 올라왔다. 우리는 아무것도 만지지 않았다. 문간에서 보니 무거운 금속 상자 아래 전선이 눌려 있었다. 선생님은 우리를 복도로 내보내고 기술자를 부르셨다. 사진은 가짜일 수도 있었다. 하지만 연기는 진짜였다.
pages.scene: Same teen boy, short black hair, navy blazer, silver watch, and ponytailed teen girl in gray cardigan, seen safely from a school laboratory doorway. An adult woman teacher in a rust cardigan guides them into the hall. Far inside the lab a tiny wisp of smoke rises below a heavy metal box under the dormant oval gate. No flames, no injury. Mature suspenseful teal-and-amber gouache.

pages.title: The Last Minute
pages.text: During the last minute before noon, an alarm sounded inside the laboratory. The gate had its own battery. Its automatic test was still on the schedule. Through the window, we watched a blue light grow between the metal arms. I wanted to run inside. My friend caught my hand. 'Help is coming,' she said. 'Do not become another person who needs it.'
pages.translation: 열한 시 오십구 분, 실험실 안에서 경보가 울렸다. 문에는 별도의 배터리가 있었다. 자동 시험은 여전히 예정대로 시작될 참이었다. 창문 너머로 금속 팔 사이에서 푸른빛이 커지는 모습이 보였다. 나는 안으로 뛰어들고 싶었다. 친구가 내 손을 붙잡았다. '도와줄 사람이 오고 있어. 너까지 위험해지면 안 돼.'
pages.scene: Same teen boy with short black hair, navy blazer and silver watch, his ponytailed friend in gray cardigan holding his hand back in the school corridor, both watching through a lab window as blue light grows between twin metal arcs of an oval gate. Adult teacher nearby. Clear physical separation from danger, suspenseful young-adult SF gouache, teal and amber, no readable text.

pages.title: An Ordinary Hero
pages.text: The engineer entered through a separate door. Our science coach showed him the alarm control. A moment later, the blue light was no longer there. The hall became quiet. There was no grand battle, no brilliant speech. An adult had followed a clear plan, and two young people had shared what they noticed. That ordinary ending seemed worth more than a grand story about a hero.
pages.translation: 기술자가 별도의 문으로 들어갔다. 선생님이 비상 제어 장치를 가리키셨다. 잠시 뒤 푸른빛이 사라졌다. 복도가 조용해졌다. 거창한 싸움도, 멋진 연설도 없었다. 어른은 정해 둔 계획대로 움직였고, 우리 두 학생은 보고 알아챈 것을 전했다. 그 평범한 마무리가 거창한 영웅담보다 더 값지게 느껴졌다.
pages.scene: A calm adult engineer in plain work clothes and the same woman teacher in rust cardigan safely shutting down the gate at a wall control panel, fading blue light inside the lab. Through the doorway the same boy with short black hair, navy blazer, silver watch and ponytailed girl in gray cardigan wait safely in the hall. Mature cinematic gouache, relief after suspense, no flames or readable extra text.

pages.title: An Empty Future
pages.text: That afternoon, the laboratory stayed closed. I kept thinking about the date on the photograph. If tomorrow had already happened, why could we change anything? My friend had another question. 'Who wrote the note?' I looked at my hand. The writing was mine, but I had never written those words together. Tomorrow, perhaps, I would have a reason.
pages.translation: 그날 오후 실험실은 계속 닫혀 있었다. 나는 사진에 적힌 날짜를 자꾸 생각했다. 내일이 이미 일어났다면, 우리가 무언가를 바꿀 수 있었던 건 왜일까? 친구는 다른 질문을 했다. '쪽지는 누가 쓴 거지?' 나는 내 손을 바라보았다. 내 글씨가 맞았지만, 그런 문장을 쓴 적은 없었다. 어쩌면 내일은 쓸 이유가 생길지도 몰랐다.
pages.scene: Same short-black-haired teenage boy in navy blazer with silver wristwatch and ponytailed friend in gray cardigan sitting on a quiet school bench at amber sunset. He studies his own hand and an indistinct printed note. Closed laboratory windows behind them. Reflective original young-adult SF gouache, restrained emotion, teal shadows, no readable writing.

pages.title: The Return Message
pages.text: The next morning, our science coach invited us back. The gate remained without power. Only the small machine was running, without any risk on a separate system. During the night, it had recorded a message moving toward yesterday. 'We cannot send a person,' she explained. 'But perhaps we can send a picture.' Beside the machine lay a blank sheet of paper and a pen.
pages.translation: 다음 날 아침, 선생님이 우리를 다시 부르셨다. 문은 여전히 연결이 끊긴 상태였다. 작은 수신기만 별도의 안전한 장치에서 작동하고 있었다. 밤사이 수신기에는 어제를 향해 움직이는 신호가 기록되어 있었다. '사람을 보낼 수는 없어. 하지만 사진은 보낼 수 있을지도 모르지.' 기계 옆에는 빈 종이와 펜이 놓여 있었다.
pages.scene: Same woman teacher in rust cardigan, same teenage boy in navy blazer and silver watch, and ponytailed girl in gray cardigan in a bright school lab the next morning. Large oval gate visibly disconnected and dark, small brass-and-teal receiver alone on a separate desk beside a blank paper and pen. Original young-adult scientific mystery gouache, optimistic teal and amber, no readable labels.

pages.title: Tomorrow Begins Here
pages.text: I wrote the words I had received: 'Do not open the gate at noon. Ask for help.' My friend added the date. Under our science coach's close watch, the machine sent a photograph. For a second, I imagined yesterday's version of me waiting beside it. Then the screen became dark. We had not learned to control the future. We had learned to care for someone inside it.
pages.translation: 나는 받았던 문장을 썼다. '낮 열두 시에 문을 열지 마. 도와 달라고 해.' 친구가 날짜를 덧붙였다. 선생님이 주의 깊게 지켜보시는 가운데 기계가 사진을 보냈다. 잠시 나는 어제의 내가 그 기계 옆에서 기다리는 모습을 상상했다. 그러고는 화면이 꺼졌다. 우리는 미래를 지배하는 법을 배운 게 아니었다. 그 미래를 살아갈 누군가를 보살피는 법을 배웠다.
pages.scene: Same teen boy with short black hair, navy blazer and silver wristwatch writes a short note at a school lab desk, ponytailed friend in gray cardigan beside him, woman teacher in rust cardigan supervising. Compact brass-and-teal receiver gives one gentle amber pulse; disconnected oval gate remains dark in background. Hopeful original young-adult SF gouache, sunrise light, no legible note lettering beyond the poem-card text.

pages.title: Between Two Stops
pages.text:
The bus carries a hundred plans.
One window holds the evening sky.
One person leaves; another stays.
The city changes as we pass.

I do not know my final stop.
Today, one small step is enough.
Between the place I leave and find,
there is still room to change my mind.
pages.translation:
버스는 수많은 계획을 싣고 달려요.
창 하나에 저녁 하늘이 담겨요.
낯선 누군가는 내리고, 또 누군가는 남아요.
우리가 지나가는 동안 도시도 달라져요.

마지막으로 내릴 곳은 아직 몰라요.
오늘은 작은 한 걸음이면 충분해요.
떠나는 곳과 새로 찾는 곳 사이에는
마음을 바꿀 여지도 남아 있어요.
pages.scene: Mature original editorial gouache, muted blue and amber. A Korean teenage girl with a short black bob and a plain olive school jacket sits beside a bus window at dusk. Restrained thoughtful mood, no childish mascots. Scene: Bus interior, teenage girl beside a rain-speckled window with city reflections and a sunset sky, a few quiet passengers.

pages.title: A Place for My Voice
pages.text:
My voice was once a folded note,
a quiet thought inside a book.
I feared the space before a crowd,
the sudden turn of every look.

Today I speak one simple truth.
My hands still shake; my words are small.
A voice need not become a shout
to have a place among us all.
pages.translation:
내 목소리는 한때 접어 둔 쪽지였어요.
책 속에 넣어 둔 조용한 생각이었죠.
사람들 앞에 선 그 공간과
일제히 돌아오는 시선이 두려웠어요.

오늘 나는 소박한 진심 하나를 말해요.
손은 여전히 떨리고, 말도 작지만요.
목소리가 꼭 외침이 되어야만
우리 사이에 자리를 얻는 것은 아니에요.
pages.scene: Original young-adult literary gouache in indigo, dusty rose and cream. A Korean teenage boy with round glasses, straight black hair and a gray sweater. Sensitive confident growth, simple school stage, no logos. Scene: Teen boy with round glasses standing at a small school stage microphone, hands lightly shaking, warm spotlight and a listening audience in soft focus.

pages.title: The Habit
pages.text: I used to reach for my phone whenever I had a free moment. A short wait became a chance to check another video. I called it rest, but I often felt more tired after the video. One afternoon, the battery ran out on my way home. For the first time that week, I had nothing to watch except the street.
pages.translation: 잠깐의 여유만 생기면 나는 휴대전화에 손을 뻗곤 했다. 잠깐 기다릴 때도 영상을 하나 더 찾아봤다. 쉬는 거라고 생각했지만, 보고 나면 더 피곤할 때가 많았다. 어느 오후 집으로 가던 길에 배터리가 다 닳았다. 그 주 들어 처음으로 눈앞의 거리만 바라보며 걸었다.
pages.scene: Original teenage editorial gouache, natural sage and warm amber palette. A Korean teenage girl with a black ponytail, cream sweatshirt and dark green backpack. Contemporary everyday life, mature restrained illustration. Scene: Teen girl on a sidewalk holding a phone with a dark screen, afternoon city around her, noticing the surroundings.

pages.title: Small Details
pages.text: I noticed a crack in the wall, a bird carrying a piece of grass, and a neighbor whose name I had never asked. We talked beside the gate. Nothing grand happened, yet the walk felt longer and richer. My attention was no longer moving from one bright picture to the next. It had time to stay somewhere.
pages.translation: 벽의 갈라진 틈과 풀잎을 물고 가는 새, 이름조차 물어본 적 없던 이웃이 눈에 들어왔다. 우리는 문 옆에서 이야기를 나눴다. 특별한 일은 없었지만, 그 산책은 더 길고 풍성하게 느껴졌다. 밝은 화면을 쉴 새 없이 넘기던 눈길이 이제는 한곳에 가만히 머물 수 있었다.
pages.scene: Original teenage editorial gouache, natural sage and warm amber palette. A Korean teenage girl with a black ponytail, cream sweatshirt and dark green backpack. Contemporary everyday life, mature restrained illustration. Scene: Same girl talking with an older woman neighbor beside a garden gate, a small bird carrying grass and textured wall nearby, phone away.

pages.title: A Choice, Not a Rule
pages.text: I still like films and messages from friends. I do not need to fight technology. I need to choose how I use it. Now I leave my phone inside my bag during one short walk each day. Some days I notice very little. Even then, the quiet is mine, and I return home with room for another thought.
pages.translation: 나는 여전히 영화와 친구들의 메시지를 즐긴다. 기술을 멀리할 필요는 없다. 내가 어떻게 쓸지 정하면 된다. 이제 나는 매일 짧게 산책하는 동안 휴대전화를 가방 안에 둔다. 별다른 것을 발견하지 못하는 날도 있다. 그런 날에도 조용히 나만의 시간을 보낸다. 집으로 돌아올 때면 새로운 생각을 할 여유가 생긴다.
pages.scene: Original teenage editorial gouache, natural sage and warm amber palette. A Korean teenage girl with a black ponytail, cream sweatshirt and dark green backpack. Contemporary everyday life, mature restrained illustration. Scene: Same girl walking home through a small green park at sunset, closed backpack, relaxed expression, no phone in hand.

pages.title: The Simple Answer
pages.text: When a friend asked me to design a poster for our club, I said yes before checking my schedule. I already had homework and a family visit that weekend. I wanted to seem kind. Instead, I became anxious. Every new message felt like another duty, and I began to blame my friend for a promise I had made.
pages.translation: 친구가 동아리 포스터를 만들어 달라고 했을 때, 나는 일정을 확인하기도 전에 좋다고 했다. 그 주말에는 숙제도 해야 했고 가족을 만나러 갈 약속도 있었다. 친절한 사람으로 보이고 싶었다. 하지만 마음은 불안해졌다. 새 메시지마다 일이 더 생기는 것 같았고, 내가 한 약속인데도 친구를 탓하기 시작했다.
pages.scene: Original young-adult editorial gouache, muted lavender, navy and warm cream. A Korean teenage boy with short slightly curly black hair and a rust sweater, and a friend with straight black hair and navy cardigan. Respectful everyday school atmosphere. Scene: Teen boy with curly black hair and rust sweater at a school desk looking overwhelmed by a calendar, notebook and poster sketches, friend nearby.

pages.title: An Honest Talk
pages.text: The next day, I explained that I could not finish the whole poster. My voice shook because I expected a fight. My friend was quiet for a moment. Then he asked which part I could manage. We divided the work. I would draw one picture; another member would prepare the text. An honest answer gave us a practical plan.
pages.translation: 다음 날, 나는 포스터 전체를 완성할 수 없다고 설명했다. 다투게 될 것 같아 목소리가 떨렸다. 친구는 잠시 조용히 있었다. 그러더니 어떤 부분을 맡을 수 있는지 물었다. 우리는 일을 나눴다. 나는 그림 하나를 그리고, 다른 부원이 글을 준비하기로 했다. 솔직하게 말하니 우리가 해낼 수 있는 방법이 보였다.
pages.scene: Original young-adult editorial gouache, muted lavender, navy and warm cream. A Korean teenage boy with short slightly curly black hair and a rust sweater, and a friend with straight black hair and navy cardigan. Respectful everyday school atmosphere. Scene: Same two teenage boys having an honest calm conversation over a poster at a school club table, dividing work with simple sketches.

pages.title: Respect for Both People
pages.text: Saying no can still feel difficult. Someone may be disappointed, and I still need to be responsible for my promises. But respect cannot mean giving away all my time. I can listen, explain my limits, and offer what I can do with care. Friends grow closer when both people have room to speak with care.
pages.translation: 거절하는 일은 여전히 쉽지 않다. 누군가는 실망할 수 있고, 나 역시 약속에 책임을 져야 한다. 하지만 친구를 존중한다고 해서 내 시간을 전부 내줘야 하는 건 아니다. 친구의 말을 듣고, 내가 어디까지 할 수 있는지 솔직히 말한 뒤, 도울 수 있는 일을 정성껏 제안하면 된다. 서로 마음을 편하게 이야기할 수 있을 때 친구 사이는 더 가까워진다.
pages.scene: Original young-adult editorial gouache, muted lavender, navy and warm cream. A Korean teenage boy with short slightly curly black hair and a rust sweater, and a friend with straight black hair and navy cardigan. Respectful everyday school atmosphere. Scene: Same two friends smiling beside a completed shared club poster, late afternoon school window light, balanced teamwork rather than one person doing everything.

pages.title: A Small Duty
pages.text: Our mountain school stood above a narrow river. I trained every morning, hoping to win the coming contest. Yet my master gave me a new duty: watch the old bridge during the village festival. I thought she had forgotten my skill. While others prepared for a match, I would count carts and guide children across a quiet piece of wood.
pages.translation: 우리 수련장은 좁은 강이 내려다보이는 산에 있었다. 나는 다가오는 대회에서 이기려고 매일 아침 수련했다. 하지만 사부님은 다른 일을 맡기셨다. 마을 축제 동안 오래된 다리를 지키라는 것이었다. 내 실력을 잊으신 걸까 싶었다. 다른 이들이 대련을 준비할 때, 나는 수레를 세고 아이들이 나무다리를 건너도록 안내해야 했다.
pages.scene: Entirely original historical martial-arts fantasy for teenage readers, cinematic literary gouache, misty jade mountains and warm gold light, no references to existing franchises. Recurring protagonist: an East Asian teenage boy with black hair tied low, indigo training robes, gray cloth belt and a plain wooden staff. His master: an elderly East Asian woman with white hair, dark green outer robe and a wooden cane. Rival: an East Asian teenage girl with braided black hair and ivory training robes. Non-graphic martial arts, no gore, no recognizable emblems. Scene: Indigo-robed teenage guard carrying a plain wooden staff at an old wooden footbridge below a mountain training school, festival village far beyond, elderly woman master assigning a task.

pages.title: The Other Guard
pages.text: A girl in white passed the bridge with a training staff. Last spring, her quick turn had stopped my attack before I could move again. 'Still guarding the road?' she asked. I heard a challenge in her voice, although she was only asking a question. Pride can turn an ordinary sentence into a battle before anyone raises a hand.
pages.translation: 흰옷을 입은 소녀가 수련용 봉을 들고 다리를 지나갔다. 지난봄, 그녀는 재빠르게 몸을 돌려 내가 다시 움직이기도 전에 공격을 막았다. '아직도 길을 지키고 있어?' 단지 질문이었는데도 내게는 도전처럼 들렸다. 자존심이 앞서면 아무도 주먹을 들지 않았는데 평범한 말 한마디에도 싸움이 시작된다.
pages.scene: Entirely original historical martial-arts fantasy for teenage readers, cinematic literary gouache, misty jade mountains and warm gold light, no references to existing franchises. Recurring protagonist: an East Asian teenage boy with black hair tied low, indigo training robes, gray cloth belt and a plain wooden staff. His master: an elderly East Asian woman with white hair, dark green outer robe and a wooden cane. Rival: an East Asian teenage girl with braided black hair and ivory training robes. Non-graphic martial arts, no gore, no recognizable emblems. Scene: Indigo-robed boy and ivory-robed braided teenage girl meeting at a mountain bridge, each with a plain wooden staff, restrained tension, no fighting or injury.

pages.title: The First Test
pages.text: At noon, the sky turned dark. Rain struck the roof of the little shelter beside the bridge. A farmer arrived with two children and a heavy cart. He needed to reach the village before the river rose. I wanted to leave for the contest. Then I remembered the first rule of our school: notice what is in front of you.
pages.translation: 정오가 되자 하늘이 어두워졌다. 빗줄기가 다리 옆 작은 쉼터의 지붕을 때렸다. 농부가 아이 둘과 무거운 수레를 끌고 왔다. 강물이 불어나기 전에 마을에 가야 했다. 나는 대회에 가고 싶었다. 그때 수련장의 첫 번째 규칙이 떠올랐다. 눈앞에 있는 것을 살피라는 것이었다.
pages.scene: Entirely original historical martial-arts fantasy for teenage readers, cinematic literary gouache, misty jade mountains and warm gold light, no references to existing franchises. Recurring protagonist: an East Asian teenage boy with black hair tied low, indigo training robes, gray cloth belt and a plain wooden staff. His master: an elderly East Asian woman with white hair, dark green outer robe and a wooden cane. Rival: an East Asian teenage girl with braided black hair and ivory training robes. Non-graphic martial arts, no gore, no recognizable emblems. Scene: Storm gathering over wooden bridge, teenage guard under a small shelter, farmer with two children and a loaded cart approaching, gray rain and jade mountains.

pages.title: A Change of Plan
pages.text: One wheel caught between two boards. The cart stopped, and a child began to cry. I could not move the weight alone. The girl in white had returned for her forgotten bag. Without another word, she put it down and joined me. Our training had taught us balance, but now we needed something less grand: a plan and another pair of hands.
pages.translation: 바퀴 하나가 널빤지 사이에 끼었다. 수레가 멈추자 아이가 울기 시작했다. 나 혼자서는 무게를 감당할 수 없었다. 흰옷의 소녀가 두고 간 가방을 찾으러 돌아왔다. 그녀는 말없이 가방을 내려놓고 곁에 섰다. 수련을 하며 균형 잡는 법은 배웠다. 하지만 지금 필요한 건 거창한 기술이 아니었다. 어떻게 옮길지 의논하고 함께 힘을 보태 줄 사람이 필요했다.
pages.scene: Entirely original historical martial-arts fantasy for teenage readers, cinematic literary gouache, misty jade mountains and warm gold light, no references to existing franchises. Recurring protagonist: an East Asian teenage boy with black hair tied low, indigo training robes, gray cloth belt and a plain wooden staff. His master: an elderly East Asian woman with white hair, dark green outer robe and a wooden cane. Rival: an East Asian teenage girl with braided black hair and ivory training robes. Non-graphic martial arts, no gore, no recognizable emblems. Scene: A cart wheel caught at a gap on the bridge, boy in indigo and girl in ivory assessing the situation together, farmer keeping children safely on the bank, no dangerous acrobatics.

pages.title: The Other Match
pages.text: We called the village people from the shelter. Together, the adults freed the wheel while we kept the children away from the broken boards. Across the valley, the contest bell rang. I knew my match was starting without me. The girl heard it too. She looked toward the school, then turned back to the child who was afraid beside her.
pages.translation: 우리는 쉼터에서 마을 사람들을 불렀다. 어른들이 힘을 합쳐 바퀴를 빼는 동안, 우리는 아이들이 부서진 널빤지에서 떨어져 있게 했다. 계곡 너머에서 대회 종이 울렸다. 내가 없는 채로 대련이 시작되고 있었다. 소녀도 들었다. 그녀는 수련장 쪽을 바라보다가 곁에서 겁먹은 아이에게 다시 고개를 돌렸다.
pages.scene: Entirely original historical martial-arts fantasy for teenage readers, cinematic literary gouache, misty jade mountains and warm gold light, no references to existing franchises. Recurring protagonist: an East Asian teenage boy with black hair tied low, indigo training robes, gray cloth belt and a plain wooden staff. His master: an elderly East Asian woman with white hair, dark green outer robe and a wooden cane. Rival: an East Asian teenage girl with braided black hair and ivory training robes. Non-graphic martial arts, no gore, no recognizable emblems. Scene: Adults helping move the stranded cart while teenage boy and girl keep two children safely near the shelter, distant mountain school bell tower visible through rain.

pages.title: After the Rain
pages.text: By evening, everyone had reached the village. My staff was covered in mud, and there was no prize waiting for either of us. My master arrived carrying a basket of dry clothes. She had been helping families along the river. She did not ask who had won. She asked whether anyone was still away, and we checked the village list together.
pages.translation: 저녁이 되자 모두 마을에 도착했다. 내 봉에는 진흙이 묻어 있었고, 우리 둘을 기다리는 상도 없었다. 사부님이 마른 옷을 담은 바구니를 들고 오셨다. 강가의 가족들을 돕고 계셨다고 했다. 누가 이겼는지보다 아직 돌아오지 않은 사람이 있는지 물으셨고, 우리는 함께 마을 명단을 확인했다.
pages.scene: Entirely original historical martial-arts fantasy for teenage readers, cinematic literary gouache, misty jade mountains and warm gold light, no references to existing franchises. Recurring protagonist: an East Asian teenage boy with black hair tied low, indigo training robes, gray cloth belt and a plain wooden staff. His master: an elderly East Asian woman with white hair, dark green outer robe and a wooden cane. Rival: an East Asian teenage girl with braided black hair and ivory training robes. Non-graphic martial arts, no gore, no recognizable emblems. Scene: Elderly woman master in green robe bringing dry clothes to the village shelter after rain, muddy indigo-robed boy and ivory-robed girl checking a list with villagers, gentle lamplight.

pages.title: What the Lesson Meant
pages.text: I at last admitted that I had wanted a chance to prove my power. My master sat beside the door. 'Power gives you a choice,' she said. 'It does not choose for you.' The girl leaned her staff against the wall. For the first time, I wondered what she had hoped to win. I asked, and this time I listened to her answer.
pages.translation: 마침내 나는 내 힘을 증명할 기회를 원했다고 털어놓았다. 사부님은 문 옆에 앉으셨다. '힘은 선택할 기회를 줄 뿐, 대신 선택해 주지는 않는다.' 소녀가 봉을 벽에 기대었다. 나는 처음으로 그녀가 무엇을 얻고 싶었을지 궁금해졌다. 물어보았고, 이번에는 답에 귀를 기울였다.
pages.scene: Entirely original historical martial-arts fantasy for teenage readers, cinematic literary gouache, misty jade mountains and warm gold light, no references to existing franchises. Recurring protagonist: an East Asian teenage boy with black hair tied low, indigo training robes, gray cloth belt and a plain wooden staff. His master: an elderly East Asian woman with white hair, dark green outer robe and a wooden cane. Rival: an East Asian teenage girl with braided black hair and ivory training robes. Non-graphic martial arts, no gore, no recognizable emblems. Scene: Quiet conversation in a traditional village shelter, elderly master seated by door, indigo-robed boy listening to the ivory-robed girl, wooden staffs resting against wall, warm evening light.

pages.title: The Next Morning
pages.text: The next morning, we returned to the bridge with the village people. While the adults repaired the damage, we carried light supplies and watched the road. There would be another contest. For now, the girl showed me the turn that had stopped me in spring. We practiced on safe ground, slowly, and laughed when both of us lost our balance.
pages.translation: 다음 날 아침, 우리는 마을 사람들과 다리로 돌아갔다. 어른들이 부서진 곳을 고치는 동안 가벼운 물품을 나르고 길을 살폈다. 대회는 또 열릴 것이다. 지금은 소녀가 지난봄 나를 이겼던 몸 돌리기를 보여 주었다. 안전한 땅에서 천천히 연습하다 둘 다 균형을 잃자 함께 웃었다.
pages.scene: Entirely original historical martial-arts fantasy for teenage readers, cinematic literary gouache, misty jade mountains and warm gold light, no references to existing franchises. Recurring protagonist: an East Asian teenage boy with black hair tied low, indigo training robes, gray cloth belt and a plain wooden staff. His master: an elderly East Asian woman with white hair, dark green outer robe and a wooden cane. Rival: an East Asian teenage girl with braided black hair and ivory training robes. Non-graphic martial arts, no gore, no recognizable emblems. Scene: Bright morning after rain, adults repairing bridge in background, indigo-robed boy and ivory-robed girl lightly practicing staff balance together on broad safe grassy ground, friendly laughter, mountains clearing.

title: A Second Life, A Small Choice

pages.title: Another Face
pages.text: In my first life, I was always waiting to become someone with great power. Then I woke in a palace with another face in the mirror. People called me prince. My old memories remained, but my body and my name belonged to this strange country. I searched for a magic power. All I found was a blank notebook and the same fear of choosing wrong.
pages.translation: 첫 번째 삶에서 나는 늘 중요한 사람이 될 날을 기다렸다. 그런데 궁전에서 눈을 떴을 때, 거울에는 다른 얼굴이 비쳤다. 사람들은 나를 왕자라고 불렀다. 예전 기억은 남아 있었지만 몸도 이름도 이 낯선 나라에서 얻은 것이었다. 특별한 힘을 찾아보았다. 발견한 것은 빈 공책과, 여전히 잘못된 선택을 할까 두려워하는 마음뿐이었다.
pages.scene: Original coming-of-age second-life fantasy for teenagers, literary gouache, copper, sage and warm cream palette, invented historical setting with no existing franchise references. Recurring narrator: East Asian teenage prince with black hair half tied using a dark green ribbon, simple pale gold robe, carrying a small red notebook. Recurring clerk: older East Asian woman with gray-streaked hair in a dark blue robe. Grounded compassionate story, no violence or copied costumes or emblems. Scene: Teenage prince with half-tied black hair, green ribbon and pale gold robe looking at an unfamiliar reflection in a palace mirror, blank red notebook on a nearby desk, soft morning light.

pages.title: The Empty Market
pages.text: At my first council meeting, an officer reported that a village had not sent its food to the city. 'They ignore our orders,' he said. I almost agreed because everyone else did. Then a quiet clerk mentioned an empty cart returning from the road. I asked what the driver had seen. Nobody in the room knew the answer.
pages.translation: 처음 참석한 회의에서 한 관리가 어느 마을이 도시에 식량을 보내지 않았다고 보고했다. '우리 명령을 무시하고 있습니다.' 모두 동의하기에 나도 그러려 했다. 그때 조용한 서기가 길에서 빈 수레가 돌아왔다고 말했다. 나는 수레를 몰던 사람이 무엇을 보았는지 물었다. 방 안에는 답을 아는 사람이 없었다.
pages.scene: Original coming-of-age second-life fantasy for teenagers, literary gouache, copper, sage and warm cream palette, invented historical setting with no existing franchise references. Recurring narrator: East Asian teenage prince with black hair half tied using a dark green ribbon, simple pale gold robe, carrying a small red notebook. Recurring clerk: older East Asian woman with gray-streaked hair in a dark blue robe. Grounded compassionate story, no violence or copied costumes or emblems. Scene: Pale-gold-robed prince at a modest palace council table, officials with papers, older blue-robed woman clerk quietly pointing to an empty-cart report, prince holding red notebook.

pages.title: A Question from Before
pages.text: In my old life, I often copied answers without understanding the question. I did not want to repeat that habit. With support from the court, I joined the clerk on a visit to the market. We found the driver beside his cart. He did not seem upset. He looked tired. 'I followed the map,' he told us. 'There was no village at the end.'
pages.translation: 예전 삶에서 나는 질문을 이해하지 않은 채 답을 베끼곤 했다. 그 습관을 되풀이하고 싶지 않았다. 궁정의 도움을 받아 서기와 함께 시장을 찾았다. 수레 옆에서 그 사람을 만났다. 화가 났다기보다 지쳐 보였다. '지도대로 갔습니다. 그런데 길 끝에 마을이 없었습니다.'
pages.scene: Original coming-of-age second-life fantasy for teenagers, literary gouache, copper, sage and warm cream palette, invented historical setting with no existing franchise references. Recurring narrator: East Asian teenage prince with black hair half tied using a dark green ribbon, simple pale gold robe, carrying a small red notebook. Recurring clerk: older East Asian woman with gray-streaked hair in a dark blue robe. Grounded compassionate story, no violence or copied costumes or emblems. Scene: Prince and older blue-robed woman clerk listening respectfully to an exhausted cart driver in a quiet historical market, a paper map and empty cart, red notebook visible.

pages.title: The Old Map
pages.text: The clerk spread the map across a table. Its date was several years old. After a flood, the village had moved to higher ground. The new address had reached one office but not another. The driver had traveled to an empty field. I had imagined a secret enemy. Instead, we had found a lost message between two ordinary rooms.
pages.translation: 서기가 탁자에 지도를 펼쳤다. 몇 년 전 날짜가 적혀 있었다. 홍수 뒤에 마을은 더 높은 곳으로 옮겨 갔다. 새 주소는 한 부서에는 전달됐지만 다른 부서에는 전달되지 않았다. 수레를 몰던 사람은 빈 들판에 갔던 것이다. 나는 숨은 적을 상상했지만, 알고 보니 두 부서 사이에서 소식이 제대로 전해지지 않은 것이었다.
pages.scene: Original coming-of-age second-life fantasy for teenagers, literary gouache, copper, sage and warm cream palette, invented historical setting with no existing franchise references. Recurring narrator: East Asian teenage prince with black hair half tied using a dark green ribbon, simple pale gold robe, carrying a small red notebook. Recurring clerk: older East Asian woman with gray-streaked hair in a dark blue robe. Grounded compassionate story, no violence or copied costumes or emblems. Scene: Older clerk and young prince comparing an old paper map and records at a simple market table, an empty field sketched on map, red notebook and small wooden markers, no readable labels.

pages.title: People Beyond the Paper
pages.text: At the village, food was ready inside the store. Families had been waiting for a cart from the city. They had sent requests, but each reply had traveled to the old address. An old woman offered us tea. I wrote down her words with care. For the first time since waking in the palace, I stopped thinking about how a prince should appear.
pages.translation: 마을의 창고에는 식량이 준비되어 있었다. 가족들은 도시에서 올 수레를 기다리고 있었다. 요청을 보냈지만 답장은 매번 예전 주소로 갔다. 할머니 한 분이 차를 내주셨다. 나는 그분의 말을 정성껏 적었다. 궁전에서 눈뜬 뒤 처음으로 왕자답게 보여야 한다는 생각을 내려놓았다.
pages.scene: Original coming-of-age second-life fantasy for teenagers, literary gouache, copper, sage and warm cream palette, invented historical setting with no existing franchise references. Recurring narrator: East Asian teenage prince with black hair half tied using a dark green ribbon, simple pale gold robe, carrying a small red notebook. Recurring clerk: older East Asian woman with gray-streaked hair in a dark blue robe. Grounded compassionate story, no violence or copied costumes or emblems. Scene: Prince seated humbly with village families beside a food store with baskets of rice, older village woman offering tea, blue-robed clerk listening, red notebook open, warm human scene.

pages.title: One Small Test
pages.text: The clerk did not suggest a grand new system. We changed one route, checked one address, and asked a driver to report what happened. I wanted to announce success at once. She shook her head. 'First, wait for the cart to return.' That afternoon, it came back full. The driver also carried a letter from the village, asking when the next visit would be.
pages.translation: 서기는 거창한 새 제도를 제안하지 않았다. 우리는 수레가 다니는 길을 바꾸고 주소를 확인한 뒤, 수레를 몰던 사람에게 다녀와서 어땠는지 알려 달라고 했다. 나는 당장 성공을 알리고 싶었다. 서기는 고개를 저었다. '먼저 수레가 돌아올 때까지 기다리세요.' 그날 오후 수레가 가득 차 돌아왔다. 다음 방문을 묻는 마을의 편지도 실려 있었다.
pages.scene: Original coming-of-age second-life fantasy for teenagers, literary gouache, copper, sage and warm cream palette, invented historical setting with no existing franchise references. Recurring narrator: East Asian teenage prince with black hair half tied using a dark green ribbon, simple pale gold robe, carrying a small red notebook. Recurring clerk: older East Asian woman with gray-streaked hair in a dark blue robe. Grounded compassionate story, no violence or copied costumes or emblems. Scene: Prince with red notebook and blue-robed clerk waiting by city gate as a cart full of food returns, driver holding a small letter, sunny hopeful historical city, no grand ceremony.

pages.title: The Wrong Kind of Prize
pages.text: Back at the palace, an officer admired my brilliant plan. I felt the old desire to seem great. Then I looked at the clerk, the driver, and the people waiting beyond the gate. 'It was not only my plan,' I said. I explained who had asked, listened, checked, and carried the food. The story sounded less like a tale and more like work.
pages.translation: 궁전으로 돌아오자 한 관리가 내 훌륭한 계획을 칭찬했다. 중요한 사람처럼 보이고 싶던 예전 욕심이 고개를 들었다. 그때 서기와 수레를 몰던 사람, 문밖에서 기다리는 사람들이 보였다. '저 혼자의 계획이 아니었습니다.' 누가 묻고, 듣고, 확인하고, 식량을 날랐는지 설명했다. 말하고 보니 거창한 전설보다는 함께 일한 이야기에 가까웠다.

pages.title: A New Beginning
pages.text: That night, I opened my notebook beneath a small lamp. I still did not know why I had received another life. No hidden power had appeared, and tomorrow would bring other problems. But I no longer needed to wait before helping other people. At the bottom of the page, I wrote one question: 'Whose answer have I not heard yet?'
pages.translation: 그날 밤 작은 등불 아래에서 공책을 펼쳤다. 왜 또 한 번의 삶을 얻었는지는 여전히 몰랐다. 숨겨진 힘도 나타나지 않았고, 내일은 또 다른 문제가 생길 것이다. 하지만 쓸모 있는 일을 시작하려고 더 기다릴 필요는 없었다. 종이 맨 아래에 질문 하나를 적었다. '아직 누구의 이야기를 듣지 못했을까?'
